questions.prompt: Which term describes a network covering a small geographic area?
questions.explanation: A local area network covers a small area; a WAN spans greater distances, and a router connects IP networks.

questions.prompt: Select all statements supported by the chapter.
options: A LAN covers a small geographic area.
A router forwards packets between IP networks.
A WAN is always limited to one room.
questions.explanation: The chapter defines LANs by their small geographic scope and routers by their packet-forwarding role. WANs span long distances.

questions.prompt: A company has offices in distant cities. Explain why a WAN is appropriate and what routers do.
questions.exampleAnswer: A WAN connects networks over long distances. Routers forward packets between the offices’ IP networks.
questions.explanation: Include the long geographic distance and the router’s role in forwarding packets between networks.

questions.prompt: Match each network type with its geographic scope.
questions.explanation: LAN means local area network; WAN means wide area network.

questions.prompt: A collection of eight bits is one _____.

questions.definition: A network covering a small geographic area, such as one building.
A network spanning long geographic distances.
A device that forwards packets between IP networks.
